Dental implant surgery

Many trials report less early pain or swelling, while a sham-controlled trial found similar symptom improvement with and without PBM. Any benefit may be short-term.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Many trials report less early pain or swelling, while a sham-controlled trial found similar symptom improvement with and without PBM. Any benefit may be short-term.

Summary of the Evidence

Twelve human reports are indexed under postoperative complications: 11 randomized trials and one non-randomized self-controlled pilot. The database does not identify overlapping cohorts. No animal or in-vitro/ex-vivo study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

Most trials report less immediate pain or swelling and/or improved early soft-tissue healing, but one 62-participant sham-controlled trial found pain and inflammation declined similarly with or without PBM; a 60-participant trial found analgesic effects converged after day 1. Follow-up is generally short and protocols vary, so benefit appears uncertain and may be time-limited (Collado-Murcia et al. 2024; Abdelsalam et al., 2026; Sun et al., 2026). Most trials follow patients for days to weeks and evaluate postoperative pain, swelling, or early soft-tissue healing rather than long-term implant survival. In the sham-controlled comparisons, any separation can be concentrated in the earliest hours and converge after the first day, suggesting that the temporal window matters. Differences in wavelength, exposure schedules, and co-interventions make the results difficult to combine into one protocol.

Primary original studies: Caccianiga et al. 2020 Collado-Murcia et al. 2024

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Caccianiga et al. used the ATP38 spectral-light device, reported across a 450–835 nm band. This spans visible blue/red wavelengths and shorter near-infrared wavelengths; it is not a single monochromatic wavelength. Other trials use different devices and schedules. The parameter range is study-specific and does not establish a standard postoperative protocol.

Interpretation

Most trials measure symptoms over days or weeks rather than implant survival or late complications. Differences in device spectrum, treatment timing, and co-interventions limit comparisons. In a sham-controlled study, similar symptom trajectories with and without PBM weaken claims of a consistent independent benefit.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow. Most reports suggest short-term relief, but sham-controlled findings include no added effect.
Publications and records12 unique titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The postoperative literature includes mostly randomized clinical reports with short follow-up. Many report less early pain, swelling, or improved healing, while a sham-controlled implant-surgery trial found pain and inflammation declined similarly with and without PBM. Protocols and outcomes vary, so a general benefit or durable effect is not established.
